proposals.evidence: Turner’s section 3 *kṣaṭ/*kṣvaṭ gives Khowar c̣hoi, Bengali chay, Kumaoni chai, Western Pahari chɔ, Gujarati cha and Marathi sahā/sā. The selected forms belong to these named regional affricate or western sahā families, including ordinary source c/ts spelling, deaspiration and contracted h/v variants. They are kept separate from the northwestern ṣuvaṭ branch; added classifier material is excluded.

proposals.evidence: Full aṣṭā/aṣṭau includes Khowar oṣṭ, Bashkarik ac̣, Torwali/Maiya āṭh and the widespread plains āṭh/āṭha series. These selected whole numeral responses fit the named branches, retaining the source’s palatal, retroflex/dental and aspiration notation and final nominal vowel. The n-initial forms filed under eight, which resemble nine, are excluded as gloss/alignment problems; classifier phrases are also excluded.
